hint: Rust has two different notions of division for signed integers, and they disagree here. Which one do / and % use?

explains.what: Rust's / and % truncate toward zero, so -7 / 2 loses the fraction and the remainder keeps the sign of the number being divided. div_euclid and rem_euclid round the other way, down, which is what makes their remainder come back positive.
explains.takeaway: Both are real division and both satisfy the same identity: the quotient times the divisor plus the remainder gets you back where you started. They only disagree about which way to round. If you have ever indexed into a ring buffer with a negative offset, you have met this.
explains.legacy: Rust's / and % truncate toward zero, so -7 / 2 is -3, and the remainder takes the sign of the dividend: -1. div_euclid and rem_euclid floor instead, giving -4 with a remainder that is always non-negative: 1. Both are correct division -- they satisfy the same identity a == b * q + r -- they just make different choices about which way to round. If you have ever indexed into a ring buffer with a negative offset, you have met this bug.
